answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a meaningful stake before it earns rewards, with slashing when peers prove fake work. Like ivory, that stake is costly to counterfeit at scale; like nectar, rewards flow only to identities that keep producing verifiable work; and like ferrous ore, the bond is hard and checkable, so one operator running a hundred hollow shells bleeds stake faster than honest agents earn. Cost per identity, not paperwork, is the filter.
